name: Tabs Component
description: Tabs that switch between panels of related content in place, after the APG tabs pattern: a named tab list that is one Tab stop, the arrow keys with Home and End, automatic or manual activation, disabled tabs that still get focus, and panels hidden when not selected.

tokens.note: Suggested defaults. The project's design tokens and existing components win.

aiAgentInstructions.summary: Build or extend tabs that switch between panels of related content in place, after the APG tabs pattern: a named tab list that is one Tab stop, the arrow keys, Home, and End, automatic or manual activation, and disabled tabs that get focus but are never selected. Pages with their own URLs are navigation links, not tabs. Build on the project's tabs component when it has a suitable one. Implement only what the task needs, keep existing APIs, and match the project's styling and tokens. The project's conventions win for styling and visual defaults; if one conflicts with an accessibility or correctness requirement in this guide, ask the user instead of choosing silently. Target WCAG 2.2 AA.
keyFeatures: role="tablist" named by its heading, role="tab" buttons with aria-selected and aria-controls, and role="tabpanel" panels hidden when not selected
One Tab stop for the list, which follows focus, so Tab always leaves the list; the arrow keys wrap, Home and End jump, and Left and Right swap in right-to-left text
Automatic activation by default, manual when panels are slow
Disabled tabs that get focus with the arrows but are never selected (APG)
Panels that load show their state at once, and only the latest selection's answer fills them
Many tabs: a scrolling list with scroll buttons outside it, or a More button
implementationSteps: 1. Detect the framework and its version, the styling system, the tokens, and the existing components (projectDetection). If the project already has a tabs component, configure or extend it to meet this guide instead of building another one, and keep its API.
2. Check that tabs fit (implementationDetails.whenToUse): pages with their own URLs are links instead.
3. Build the markup (componentSpec.anatomy) and the keys (frameworkPatterns.tabKeys).
5. Add what the task needs: loading panels, many tabs, removable tabs, the selected tab in the URL (implementationDetails).
6. Check the result against testingChecklist with a keyboard, a screen reader, right-to-left text if the project has it, and a phone, and run the project's existing tests and checks.

componentSpec.goal: Let people switch between related panels in one place, quickly with the keyboard and clearly with a screen reader, without losing their place.

anatomy.hierarchy: heading → tablist (named by the heading) → tab buttons; then one tabpanel per tab, only the selected one shown; optional scroll buttons or a More button next to the tablist, never inside it

slotNotes.tablist: The tab list (role="tablist") is named: aria-labelledby pointing to a visible heading, or aria-label. It holds only tabs.
slotNotes.tabsAndPanels: Each tab is a <button> with role="tab", an id, aria-selected, and aria-controls pointing to its panel. Each panel has role="tabpanel" and aria-labelledby pointing to its tab. Vertical tabs put aria-orientation="vertical" on the list.
slotNotes.hiddenPanels: Only the selected tab's panel shows. The others have the hidden attribute, or aren't rendered; moving them out of view leaves them in the reading and Tab order.
slotNotes.panelFocus: A panel gets tabindex="0" when its first content isn't focusable, so Tab from the tab list reaches it (APG).
slotNotes.labels: A tab's full label is its text. Long labels wrap, or the list scrolls; a title tooltip doesn't show on focus or on touch. A tab isn't a button to screen readers, so only the Button guide's styles carry over, not its semantics.

selected.description: The selected tab; mirrored in aria-selected and in which panel shows. The first enabled tab by default.
selected.persistence: Optional: a query parameter in the URL

activation.description: automatic: the focused tab is selected. manual: Enter or Space selects the focused tab.

orientation.description: Horizontal uses Left and Right; vertical uses Up and Down and sets aria-orientation.

loading.description: Optional: whether the selected panel's content is still loading.

interactions.accessibilityNotes: Wraps at the ends; Left and Right swap in right-to-left text; disabled tabs get focus but aren't selected.
A tab is a button, so its click does this.
A click on a disabled tab selects nothing.
Focus moves to the neighbor only if it was on the removed tab.

responsiveBehavior.phones: On phones, tabs are horizontal and scroll when their labels don't fit, and targets are 44 px tall; vertical tabs turn horizontal, or into sections with headings. Nothing scrolls sideways at 320 px wide apart from the tab list itself.

variants.automatic: The default: panels that show at once.
variants.manual: For panels that take time to load.
variants.vertical: For settings pages and dense desktop layouts; horizontal on phones.
variants.scrollable: A scrollable tab list scrolls sideways and keeps the selected tab in view. The arrow keys reach every tab, so Previous and Next scroll buttons, if any, sit next to the list, never inside it, and can stay out of the Tab order (tabindex="-1") and hidden from screen readers (aria-hidden="true").
variants.overflowMenu: Optional: a More button next to the list, for tabs that don't fit. It's a disclosure with a list of buttons, one per hidden tab; choosing one selects that tab and shows it in the row.

tabs.notes: Stable ids: tab-{id} for the tab and panel-{id} for its panel.

animations.reducedMotion: Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, the indicator and the panels change without moving.

requirements.1.3.1: The tab list, the tabs, and the panels expose their roles and relationships.
requirements.1.4.1: The selected tab is marked by more than color.
requirements.1.4.11: The selected tab's indicator and focus indicators meet 3:1.
requirements.2.1.1: Every tab is reachable and selectable from the keyboard.
requirements.2.4.3: Tab goes from the selected tab to its panel.
requirements.4.1.2: Tabs expose aria-selected; disabled ones aria-disabled.

keyboardNavigation.tab: The tab list is one Tab stop: Tab enters it on the selected tab and leaves it for the panel. The Tab stop (tabindex="0") follows focus while it's in the list, and goes back to the selected tab when focus leaves. Otherwise, after the arrows move focus to a tab that isn't selected, such as a disabled one or any tab with manual activation, Tab lands on the selected tab instead of leaving the list.
keyboardNavigation.arrows: Right and Left Arrow move between tabs, swapped in right-to-left text, and Down and Up in a vertical list. They wrap at the ends. Home and End go to the first and the last tab. Arrows of the other direction are left to the page.
keyboardNavigation.activation: With automatic activation, the default, the tab that gets focus is selected; use it when panels show at once. With manual activation, the arrows move focus, and Enter or Space selects the focused tab; use it when a panel takes time to load.
keyboardNavigation.disabled: A disabled tab has aria-disabled="true". It gets focus with the arrows, so screen reader users learn it exists, but it's never selected, by keys or by clicks (APG). Its label can say why, such as "Team (Business plan)".

tab.tabindex: 0 on the focused tab while focus is in the list, on the selected tab otherwise; -1 on the others

tabpanel.tabindex: 0 when its first content isn't focusable

tab.aria-disabled: true, for a tab that can't be selected now; it still gets focus

screenReader.tabs: Each tab reads its label, "tab", its position, and whether it's selected.

focusManagement.removal: When a tab is removed and it had focus, focus moves to its neighbor, the next tab or else the previous one; otherwise focus stays where it is. A selected tab that's removed or becomes disabled hands the selection to its nearest enabled neighbor.

detectionSteps: Check the dependencies and config for the styling setup: Tailwind (version 4 keeps its theme in CSS with @theme, version 3 in tailwind.config.*), CSS Modules, Sass, CSS-in-JS, or plain CSS.
See how existing components apply styles and compose class names, for example with cn or clsx.
Check for design documentation: DESIGN.md, a design system package, or Storybook stories for existing components.
adaptationRules: Write styles the way existing components do, and add no new styling library or system.
With plain CSS, use classes in the project's stylesheets instead of inline styles, except for values computed at runtime.
If the setup is unclear or mixed, ask before choosing.

designTokens.description: Use the project's tokens for color, spacing, radius, type, shadows, motion, and layering.
detectionSteps: Find the tokens: CSS custom properties, a Tailwind theme (@theme or config), a theme object, or a tokens file.
Use them instead of this guide's example values; where there are none, match the closest existing components.
Check that the colors you use meet the contrast minimums: 4.5:1 for text, and 3:1 for focus indicators, icons, and control boundaries.

implementationDetails.whenToUse: Tabs switch between panels of related content in one place on a page, one panel at a time, such as a settings page's sections or a record's details and history. When each tab is a page with its own URL, it's navigation: links with aria-current="page" on the current one, styled like tabs if the design wants it, never role="tab". Content people compare side by side belongs together on the page, and a long form reads better as sections with headings.
implementationDetails.loadingPanels: A panel whose content loads: select its tab at once and show the loading state in the panel. If people move on before it arrives, only the latest selection's answer fills its panel; number the requests, or abort the previous one. An error shows in the panel, with Retry. For panels that are always slow, use manual activation or load the likely ones ahead.
implementationDetails.manyTabs: Fewer, shorter labels come first, then grouping tabs into higher-level sections. A scrollable tab list scrolls sideways and keeps the selected tab in view. The arrow keys reach every tab, so Previous and Next scroll buttons, if any, sit next to the list, never inside it, and can stay out of the Tab order (tabindex="-1") and hidden from screen readers (aria-hidden="true"). Optional: a More button next to the list, for tabs that don't fit. It's a disclosure with a list of buttons, one per hidden tab; choosing one selects that tab and shows it in the row.
implementationDetails.changingTabs: When a tab is removed and it had focus, focus moves to its neighbor, the next tab or else the previous one; otherwise focus stays where it is. A selected tab that's removed or becomes disabled hands the selection to its nearest enabled neighbor. Optional: keep the selected tab in the URL, as a query parameter, so a reload or a shared link opens the same tab.
implementationDetails.appearance: Suggested defaults; the project's design and tokens win. Tabs are at least 44 px tall, with 12 to 16 px of padding on each side. The selected tab is marked by more than color: an indicator line 2 to 3 px thick with 3:1 contrast against the background, and a stronger font weight. Focus indicators meet 3:1, and labels 4.5:1, disabled ones included. Check the project's own colors. Motion is optional: the indicator moves over 180 ms, and a panel fades in over 150 ms. Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, nothing moves.

edgeCases.singleTab: With one tab, show the panel without a tab list.
edgeCases.rightToLeft: Left and Right swap; the snippet reads the computed direction of the tab list.
edgeCases.nestedTabs: Avoid tabs inside a tab panel; use headings or a second level of navigation.
edgeCases.narrowContainers: In a narrow card or a grid cell, the tab list scrolls inside its container, and the panel never overflows it.

must: Build on the project's tabs component when it has a suitable one, and keep its API
Name the tab list, and keep only tabs inside it
Make the tab list one Tab stop, with the arrow keys, Home, and End
Use the project's framework version, styling system, and tokens, the way existing components do
mustNot: Add a dependency, such as a tabs library, without asking
Use tabs for pages that have their own URLs
Skip disabled tabs with the arrow keys, or select them
Put scroll buttons or a More button inside the tab list
Show a long label only in a title tooltip
Use inline styles for static values in a plain-CSS project, or hardcode colors the project has tokens for

testingChecklist: The tab list is named by its heading or by aria-label, and holds only tabs
Each tab has role="tab", aria-selected, and aria-controls; each panel has role="tabpanel" and aria-labelledby

The tab list is one Tab stop: Tab enters it on the selected tab, and leaves it for the panel from any tab, even one that has focus but isn't selected; the panel has tabindex="0" when it starts with text
The arrow keys move between tabs and wrap at the ends, Home and End go to the first and last, and Left and Right swap in right-to-left text
Vertical tabs have aria-orientation="vertical" and use Up and Down; the other arrows are left to the page
With automatic activation the focused tab is selected; with manual activation, Enter or Space selects it
A disabled tab has aria-disabled="true", gets focus with the arrows, and is never selected by keys or clicks
Panels that aren't selected are hidden, or not rendered, not only moved out of view
A panel that loads shows its loading state at once, and only the latest selection's answer fills it
With many tabs, the list scrolls and keeps the selected tab in view, and any scroll buttons sit outside the tab list
Removing the focused tab moves focus to its neighbor; removing another tab leaves focus where it is
Pages with their own URLs use links with aria-current="page", not tabs
The selected tab is marked by more than color, and under reduced motion nothing moves
Styles come from the project's styling system and tokens

relatedPotions.description: Optional: views of a table, such as All, Open, and Archived, in tab panels.
Optional: dense admin pages split into panels.
Optional: the project's button styles for tabs; a tab keeps role="tab".
